AD_FIELD.NAME: Indexing Enabled
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: When checked, changes to the source table are captured for indexing
AD_FIELD.HELP: Disabling it removes the generated database triggers on the next update.database.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Namespace
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Logical partition under which the embeddings of this source are stored
AD_FIELD.HELP: Must match an existing vector collection. A value with no collection fails at search time with VECTOR_COLLECTION_NOT_FOUND.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Reindex On Change
AD_FIELD.HELP: Whether a change to this column enqueues a re-embedding. Leave it off for a column that is only metadata to filter by, so editing it does not pay for an embedding that would come out the same.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A change in this column enqueues a re-embedding of the record

AD_FIELD.NAME: Sequence Number
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The order of records in a specified document.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Sequence indicates the order of records

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Last Error
AD_FIELD.HELP: What the provider or the database answered the last time this failed. It is the first thing to read when events pile up: a revoked key, a model that no longer exists and a source with no content column all stop delivery, and only this says which.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Message of the most recent failed attempt

AD_FIELD.NAME: Enqueued Records
AD_FIELD.HELP: How many records the backfill has enqueued so far. It counts events written to the outbox, not vectors stored: delivery happens afterwards, so this reaching the total only means the queue is complete, not that the index is.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: How many records this reindex has enqueued so far

AD_FIELD.NAME: Table
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A dictionary table used for this tab that points to the database table.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Table indicates the table in which a field or fields reside.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Outbox Event
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A queued indexing event

AD_FIELD.NAME: Filter Display Logic
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Expression restricting which indexed records this target returns
AD_FIELD.HELP: Uses display logic syntax over the configured metadata columns, for example @IsSOTrx@='Y'. Field names must be columns configured on the source.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Configuration Version
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Version counter of the source configuration
AD_FIELD.HELP: Every queued event carries the version it was created under. Events from an older version are discarded instead of indexed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Target
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A named, filterable entry point for vector search

AD_FIELD.NAME: Column
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A link to the database column of the table.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Link to the database column of the table

AD_FIELD.NAME: Module
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Module
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the module the element forms part of.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Last Error
AD_FIELD.HELP: What the provider or the database answered the last time this failed. It is the first thing to read when events pile up: a revoked key, a model that no longer exists and a source with no content column all stop delivery, and only this says which.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Message of the most recent failed attempt

AD_FIELD.NAME: Column
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A link to the database column of the table.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Link to the database column of the table

AD_FIELD.NAME: Event Type
AD_FIELD.HELP: What happened to the record that produced this event: INSERT and UPDATE re-embed it, DELETE removes its vector. It is written by the database trigger, never by hand.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Operation that produced the event

AD_FIELD.NAME: Status
AD_FIELD.HELP: Where the event is in delivery. PENDING is waiting, PROCESSING has been claimed by a run, DONE was embedded and stored, FAILED gave up after the provider retry limit, and SUPERSEDED was discarded because the source configuration changed after the event was enqueued and re-embedding it would have stored a vector nobody asked for. Only the scheduled process writes this: a claim is an update guarded by the previous status, so editing it by hand can hand one event to two runs at once.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Lifecycle state of the record

AD_FIELD.NAME: Column
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A link to the database column of the table.
AD_FIELD.HELP: Link to the database column of the table

AD_FIELD.NAME: Index On Update
AD_FIELD.HELP: Whether changing a watched column enqueues an event. The trigger only fires for the columns marked Reindex On Change and only when the value really changed, so a save that touches nothing else costs nothing.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Enqueue an indexing event when a watched column changes

AD_FIELD.NAME: Embedding Batch Size
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Number of texts sent per provider request
AD_FIELD.HELP: Bounds both the provider request and the transaction the scheduled process holds while delivering it.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Module
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Module
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the module the element forms part of.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Module
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Module
AD_FIELD.HELP: Indicates the module the element forms part of.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Embedding Provider
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Provider used to turn the source content into vectors
AD_FIELD.HELP: Defines the model and its dimensions. Changing it on a populated source makes the existing vectors incomparable with the new ones.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Request Timeout
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Seconds to wait for an embedding response before failing the event
AD_FIELD.HELP: How long a single embedding request may take before it is abandoned. It bounds one request, not the whole delivery run: the event it belonged to is marked as failed and retried later, up to the retry limit. Too low a value turns a slow provider into a stream of failures; too high a one holds a delivery thread while the queue grows.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Max Input Characters
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Content longer than this is truncated before embedding
AD_FIELD.HELP: Longest text sent for a single record; anything beyond this is cut off before the request leaves. It exists because a model rejects an input past its token limit and the whole batch fails with it, so one oversized record would stop the records batched alongside it. Characters are not tokens: leave room, as a token is roughly four characters for English text and fewer for other languages.

AD_FIELD.NAME: API Endpoint
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Base URL of the embeddings API. Leave empty to use the provider default
AD_FIELD.HELP: Optional. Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible embeddings API, up to and including /v1 and no further: the path of the call is added by the module and is never configured here. Leave it empty to call OpenAI itself. Point it at the Etendo LLM proxy (https://llm.etendo.software/v1), an Azure OpenAI deployment, a corporate gateway or a local stub to use the same configuration against any of them. When the endpoint is a provider-agnostic gateway, name the provider in the Embedding Model field as well.

AD_FIELD.NAME: API Key Reference
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Name of the property, environment variable or Openbravo.properties entry holding the key
AD_FIELD.HELP: This is the name of where the key lives, never the key itself. The value is stored in clear text and exported with the module dataset.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Provider Type
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Embedding backend implementation
AD_FIELD.HELP: Which API dialect the endpoint speaks. OpenAI is the only one implemented, and it is also what every OpenAI-compatible gateway serves, so it is the right choice for the Etendo LLM proxy and for an Azure OpenAI deployment as well. It is not the name of the company behind the model: that goes in the Embedding Model field when the endpoint serves several.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Embedding Model
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Provider model identifier, for example text-embedding-3-small
AD_FIELD.HELP: Model that produces the embeddings, as the endpoint names it, for instance text-embedding-3-small. A provider-agnostic gateway such as the Etendo LLM proxy serves more than one provider and has to be told which one to use: there the format is "provider/model", for instance openai/text-embedding-3-small. Changing this on a source that already has a collection does not re-embed anything, and if the new model has a different vector size the collection no longer matches -- activation reports that rather than repairing it, because repairing means dropping every vector it holds.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Embedding Content
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: When checked, the value of this column is part of the embedded text
AD_FIELD.HELP: Unchecked columns are still stored as filterable metadata, they just do not contribute to the vector.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Client
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Client for this installation.
AD_FIELD.HELP: A Client is a company or a legal entity. You cannot share data between Clients.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Organization
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Organizational entity within client
AD_FIELD.HELP: An organization is a unit of your client or legal entity - examples are store, department. You can share data between organizations.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Status
AD_FIELD.HELP: Where the event is in delivery. PENDING is waiting, PROCESSING has been claimed by a run, DONE was embedded and stored, FAILED gave up after the provider retry limit, and SUPERSEDED was discarded because the source configuration changed after the event was enqueued and re-embedding it would have stored a vector nobody asked for. Only the scheduled process writes this: a claim is an update guarded by the previous status, so editing it by hand can hand one event to two runs at once.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Lifecycle state of the record

AD_FIELD.NAME: Filter Value
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Value the filter column is compared against
AD_FIELD.HELP: Together with the filter column it restricts which records are enqueued. The comparison is compiled into the generated trigger, so changes take effect after the next update.database.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Last Enqueued Record
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Key of the last record enqueued by this reindex
AD_FIELD.HELP: The reindex walks the source table in key order and stores how far it got, so an interrupted run continues from there instead of starting over. Written by the process.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Active
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A flag indicating whether this record is available for use or de-activated.
AD_FIELD.HELP: There are two methods of making records unavailable in the system: One is to delete the record, the other is to de-activate the record. A de-activated record is not available for selection, but available for reporting. There are two reasons for de-activating and not deleting records: (1) The system requires the record for auditing purposes. (2) The record is referenced by other records. E.g., you cannot delete a Business Partner, if there are existing invoices for it. By de-activating the Business Partner you prevent it from being used in future transactions.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Index On Insert
AD_FIELD.HELP: Whether a new record enqueues an event. Turning it off leaves records created from now on out of the index until a backfill picks them up.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Enqueue an indexing event when a record is created

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Source Column
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Column of the source table contributing to the embedding

AD_FIELD.NAME: Distance Metric
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: How similarity between embeddings is measured
AD_FIELD.HELP: Cosine is the recommended default for text embeddings. It is applied when the vector collection is created.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Search Target Key
AD_FIELD.HELP: The name a caller uses to search this target through the API. It is part of the contract with whoever integrates: changing it breaks every caller already asking for the old one.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Stable identifier API clients use to select this search target

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Processed At
AD_FIELD.HELP: When delivery finished with this event, in UTC. Every timestamp the module writes is UTC rather than the session time zone, so comparing one against another is meaningful wherever the server and the client happen to be.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Moment the event reached a terminal state

AD_FIELD.NAME: Configuration Version
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Version counter of the source configuration
AD_FIELD.HELP: Every queued event carries the version it was created under. Events from an older version are discarded instead of indexed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Embedding Provider
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Provider used to turn the source content into vectors
AD_FIELD.HELP: Defines the model and its dimensions. Changing it on a populated source makes the existing vectors incomparable with the new ones.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Activate Vector Indexing
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Installs pgvector in this database and creates the collection of the selected sources
AD_FIELD.HELP: Nothing installs pgvector on its own: compiling the module, running update.database or starting the application never create an extension or a vector object. Select the sources to turn on and press this button. It installs the extension and the runtime storage once per database, and then creates the collection of each selected source using the vector size of its provider and its own distance metric. Running it again is harmless, and it is also how a source added later finishes being set up. A source that is not enabled, has no embedding provider, or already has its collection is reported and left alone, so selecting every row is a sensible way to use it.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Retry Limit
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Delivery attempts before an event stops being recovered automatically
AD_FIELD.HELP: How many times a failed event is handed back to delivery before it is left alone. It stops a permanent failure -- a model that no longer exists, a revoked key -- from being retried forever at the provider's expense. An event that reached the limit stays failed and visible in the Outbox Monitor, where it can be sent back to the queue once the cause is fixed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Table
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: A dictionary table used for this tab that points to the database table.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Table indicates the table in which a field or fields reside.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Index On Delete
AD_FIELD.HELP: Whether deleting a record removes its vector. Turning it off leaves the vectors of deleted records in the collection, where a search will keep returning them.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Remove the embedding when a record is deleted

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Dimensions
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Length of the embedding vector
AD_FIELD.HELP: Must match what the model returns. Limited to 2000, which is the ceiling for an indexable vector column.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Filter Column
AD_FIELD.HELP: Optional. Indexes only the records whose column matches Filter Value, instead of the whole table. The filter is compiled into the database trigger, so a record that does not match never reaches the queue at all -- which is also why changing it does not remove the vectors of records that matched before.
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Column of the source table compared against the filter value

AD_FIELD.NAME: Configuration Version
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Version counter of the source configuration
AD_FIELD.HELP: Every queued event carries the version it was created under. Events from an older version are discarded instead of indexed.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Record ID
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: An record identifier in the dictionary.
AD_FIELD.HELP: The Record ID is the internal unique identifier of a record

AD_FIELD.NAME: Attempt Count
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Delivery attempts so far
AD_FIELD.HELP: Compared against the retry limit of the source provider to decide whether an abandoned event is recovered or retired.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Vector Search Source
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: The vector search source this record belongs to
AD_FIELD.HELP: Identifies which table is indexed, under which namespace, and with which embedding provider.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Estimated Records
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Approximate number of records the source table holds
AD_FIELD.HELP: Taken from the table statistics once, when the reindex starts. It is an estimate meant to show progress, not an exact count: counting exactly would scan the whole table on every refresh.

AD_FIELD.NAME: Request Reindex
AD_FIELD.DESCRIPTION: Asks for the records the source already held to be indexed
AD_FIELD.HELP: The triggers only capture what changes from the moment they are installed, so a source configured over a table that already has rows indexes nothing until those rows are walked. Select the sources and press this button to ask for that walk; the scheduled process does it, in bounded chunks, so a table of millions of rows neither holds your session nor fills the queue faster than delivery drains it. The message tells you roughly how many records you just asked for. A source has one request for its whole life, so asking again starts it over and the counters of the previous walk are lost. A walk already in progress is left alone, and a source that could not be delivered is refused rather than queued.
